title: Non-Revenue Water (NRW) losses in Mumbai's distribution network
description:
MCGM's water distribution network loses a significant share of treated water daily to leakages, illegal tapping, and metering inaccuracies before it reaches consumers, despite the city drawing ~3,850-3,900 MLD from seven lakes (Tulsi, Vihar, Tansa, Modak Sagar, Upper Vaitarna, Middle Vaitarna, Bhatsa). The Mumbai City Development Plan and MCGM's own Water Supply Project documents flag ageing pipeline infrastructure, unmetered slum connections, and pressure-zone mismanagement as root causes.

Sector: Water Resources & Supply
Geographic Scope: Mumbai City (MCGM jurisdiction)
Responsible Ministry / Department: Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM) - Hydraulic Engineering Dept.
Government Source: https://www.mcgm.gov.in/irj/go/km/docs/documents/MCGM%20Department%20List/City%20Engineer/Deputy%20City%20Engineer%20(Planning%20and%20Design)/City%20Development%20Plan/Urban%20Basic%20Services.pdf
Key Verified Data Point: ~3,850-3,900 MLD drawn; documented inequitable distribution between slum and non-slum households (MCGM City Development Plan)
TCET Department(s) Mapped: CIVIL, IoT, AIDS
TRL: TRL 4-5 (lab-validated leak-detection algorithms exist; city-scale pilot needed)
MRL: MRL 4-5 (sensor hardware for pipeline retrofit is off-the-shelf; integration/ruggedization for field deployment not yet standardized)
SDG Alignment: SDG 6 (Clean Water), SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation & Infrastructure), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities)
Engineering Problem Justification: Core civil hydraulics problem (pipe network design, pressure-zone hydraulics) combined with an instrumentation/data problem (leak signature detection from acoustic/pressure sensor streams) — squarely an engineering optimization problem, not a policy-only issue.
Disciplinary Classification: Interdisciplinary — Civil (hydraulic network modeling) + IoT (sensor deployment) + AI/DS (anomaly detection on telemetry) — three distinct engineering disciplines working on one shared physical system.
Suggested Tech/Research Angle: IoT smart metering, AI-based leak/pressure anomaly detection, GIS-based pipeline health mapping
Difficulty Level: Medium-High
Source Confidence: Verified (fetched via search, official MCGM PDF)

title: Groundwater depletion and unregulated borewell extraction in Maharashtra
description:
Maharashtra's Water Resources Department and the Central Ground Water Board have flagged over-extraction of groundwater in several talukas, especially in drought-prone Marathwada and parts of Vidarbha, with falling water tables affecting irrigation and drinking water security. Urban expansion in MMR is also increasing dependence on unregulated private borewells.

Responsible Ministry / Department: Ministry of Jal Shakti - Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) / Maharashtra Water Resources Dept.

title: Drinking water quality contamination in informal settlements
description:
Informal settlements and slum clusters in Mumbai (e.g., Govandi, Mankhurd, Dharavi) frequently report contaminated water supply due to proximity of water pipelines to sewage lines and open drains, leading to waterborne disease outbreaks.

Sector: Water Resources & Supply
Geographic Scope: Mumbai (M/East, M/West wards - Govandi, Mankhurd, Deonar)
Responsible Ministry / Department: MCGM Hydraulic Engineering Dept. / Public Health Dept.
Government Source: https://www.mcgm.gov.in/

title: Sewage treatment capacity gap vs generation in Mumbai
description:
Mumbai generates sewage far exceeding the treatment capacity of its existing STPs, with large volumes of partially treated or untreated sewage discharged into the sea and rivers like the Mithi, contributing to coastal and river pollution. MCGM's Mumbai Sewage Disposal Project (MSDP) upgrades have been delayed for years.

Sector: Water Resources & Supply
Geographic Scope: Mumbai City
Responsible Ministry / Department: MCGM Sewerage Operations Dept. / Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB)
Government Source: https://mpcb.gov.in/
Key Verified Data Point: NEERI report (post-2005 floods) documented tonnes of raw sewage discharged daily into Mithi river
TCET Department(s) Mapped: CIVIL, MECH
TRL: TRL 6-7 (STP process technology itself is mature/deployed; the gap is capacity-scale-up and monitoring, not invention)
MRL: MRL 7-8 (STP equipment is commercially manufactured at scale; bottleneck is civil infrastructure build-out, not manufacturing readiness)
SDG Alignment: SDG 6 (Clean Water & Sanitation), SDG 14 (Life Below Water), SDG 11 (Sustainable Cities)

Disciplinary Classification: Multidisciplinary — Primarily Civil engineering (environmental/sanitary engineering); Mechanical contributes to treatment-plant equipment design — disciplines work in parallel rather than deeply integrated.
Suggested Tech/Research Angle: Real-time STP load monitoring dashboards, decentralized greywater recycling for housing societies
Difficulty Level: High
Source Confidence: Verified (MPCB + court records cross-referenced)

title: Rainwater harvesting non-compliance in new constructions
description:
Despite Maharashtra Regional Town Planning (MRTP) Act mandates and MCGM building bye-laws requiring rainwater harvesting (RWH) systems in buildings above a plot-size threshold, compliance and functional maintenance of RWH structures remains poor and largely unaudited across Mumbai and other Maharashtra cities.

Sector: Water Resources & Supply
Geographic Scope: Maharashtra (urban local bodies)
Responsible Ministry / Department: Urban Development Department, Government of Maharashtra
Government Source: https://urban.maharashtra.gov.in/
Key Verified Data Point: MRTP Act & Development Control Regulations mandate RWH; audit data on compliance is sparse in public domain
TCET Department(s) Mapped: CIVIL, IoT
TRL: TRL 4-5 (satellite/drone rooftop detection demonstrated in remote-sensing research; municipal-scale auditing pipeline not yet built)
MRL: N/A (auditing/monitoring system, not a manufactured product)

Disciplinary Classification: Interdisciplinary — Civil (RWH system design/compliance norms) + IoT/AIDS (remote sensing, image-based compliance detection).
Suggested Tech/Research Angle: Satellite/drone-based rooftop RWH compliance auditing, IoT tank-level sensors
Difficulty Level: Medium
Source Confidence: Standard (well-known regulation; portal is official state UD dept.)

title: Water tanker mafia and informal water markets in water-scarce wards
description:

Sector: Water Resources & Supply
Geographic Scope: Mumbai + drought-prone Maharashtra towns (Marathwada, Vidarbha)

Difficulty Level: Medium

title: Coastal saline water intrusion in Mumbai's low-lying wards
description:
Rising sea levels combined with groundwater over-extraction are causing saline intrusion in aquifers along Mumbai's coastal and low-lying wards, threatening both drinking water quality and agricultural land in nearby Konkan coastal talukas of Maharashtra, per Mumbai Climate Action Plan vulnerability assessments by WRI India.

Sector: Water Resources & Supply

Responsible Ministry / Department: Environment Department, Government of Maharashtra / BMC (MCAP)

title: Irrigation water-use inefficiency in Maharashtra's sugarcane belt
description:
Maharashtra's water-intensive sugarcane cultivation (concentrated in Western Maharashtra) consumes a disproportionate share of irrigation water relative to cropped area, contributing to water stress in drought-affected regions, a concern repeatedly raised by the state Water Resources Department and Economic Survey of Maharashtra.

Sector: Water Resources & Supply
Geographic Scope: Western Maharashtra (Kolhapur, Sangli, Solapur, Ahmednagar)

Disciplinary Classification: Interdisciplinary — Mechanical (irrigation system/actuator design) + IoT (soil-moisture sensing) + AI/DS (satellite NDWI/NDVI-based water-stress prediction).

Difficulty Level: Medium

title: Lake and reservoir siltation reducing Mumbai's water storage capacity
description:
Mumbai's supply lakes (particularly Tansa and Vihar) face gradual siltation and catchment area encroachment, reducing effective storage capacity over decades, a concern flagged in MCGM's long-term water supply planning documents including the Chitale Committee recommendations post-1992 drought scare.

Sector: Water Resources & Supply
Geographic Scope: Thane/Palghar/Nashik catchment areas feeding Mumbai lakes
Responsible Ministry / Department: MCGM Hydraulic Engineering Dept. / Irrigation Department, Maharashtra

Suggested Tech/Research Angle: Bathymetric surveying via drones/sonar, siltation-rate ML forecasting for maintenance scheduling
Difficulty Level: Medium-High

title: Flood-prone stormwater drain (nullah) desilting inefficiency
description:

title: Peak-hour traffic congestion in Mumbai Metropolitan Region
description:
Mumbai ranks among the world's most congested cities, with roughly 700,000 commuters entering Greater Mumbai daily during the morning peak hour from neighbouring municipalities, per LEA Associates' Comprehensive Mobility Plan for MCGM. Vehicular population has grown far faster than road capacity, and multiple agencies operate with limited data coordination.

Sector: Transport & Mobility
Geographic Scope: Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR)
Responsible Ministry / Department: Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA)
Government Source: https://mmrda.maharashtra.gov.in/

title: Last-mile connectivity gap from suburban railway stations
description:
Many Mumbai suburban rail stations lack safe, organized last-mile transport options, forcing commuters toward unregulated shared autos/taxis or long unsafe walks, an issue flagged in MMRDA's mobility planning studies and the Mumbai Comprehensive Mobility Plan.

title: Freight and truck movement bottlenecks at Mumbai Port/JNPT corridors
